title: Exploring contact
description: The agent changes tools and contact poses, but does not complete the task.
instruction: Fill the jar with all the coffee beans and then close it with the lid.
initial_prompt:
Complete this single task yourself using the tools: Fill the jar with all the coffee beans and then close it with the lid.
Robot: manip/lift2/R5a, two arms and a movable planar base. Left arm is left in the overlook view. EEF poses are local to each arm's planner base: +X forward, +Y robot-left, +Z up; quaternion order wxyz. Fingers extend along tool +X and open along tool Y. Wrist cameras move/rotate with the hands. Measured local EEF z is not height above the tabletop. There is no supplied depth, object pose or camera calibration. Only RGB and measured robot EEF/gripper/base state are available. Base observed yaw is radians; tool command yaw is degrees. You have one continuous conversation and may choose any continuous EEF target, both arms, base motion and waypoint batching. Use execute_eef sequentially, not parallel calls. Use observations to judge motion and object manipulation. The server determines task success independently. Do not start another episode. Resource limits: unlimited tool calls, physics deadline enforced by the server; no hard token limit; resource reminders start after 2,000,000 cumulative tokens. Resource reminders ask you to reduce unnecessary token use while continuing useful work. Select only useful camera views after the initial observation to control resource use. When finished, state the observed outcome concisely.
Manipulation guidance: after visually aligning, close at a stationary pose and allow settling. A nonzero finger gap on the table is contact evidence, not proof of a secure grasp. Test each grasp by lifting only 0.01 m first, using motion_steps=16 or more, then hold 8..16 steps and request the active wrist plus overlook views. Keep orientation and base fixed during this test. Check both finger gap and RGB to confirm the object rises with the gripper before further lifting or transport. If it remains on the table or slips, lower and adjust local contact depth/centering using current images. There is no fixed limit on failed grasp attempts; retry or change approach within the remaining experiment budgets. Avoid large instantaneous target jumps while holding an object; use motion_steps for controlled transport. Total steps per waypoint must remain <=64 and includes the ramp. Use only the active wrist for local corrections, adding overlook when establishing alignment, testing grasp, or verifying placement.
RGB inputs are downsampled: overlook 640x360, wrist 384x288; no crop or object annotation.

Align jar just below edge and approach spoon handle from above

Test spoon grasp with small vertical lift
Release holder contact and recenter on exposed spoon handle behind it
Test grasp of spoon handle by lifting one centimetre
Lift secured spoon clear and turn bowl toward bean pile
Reacquire spoon farther along handle above holder, after it slipped
Adjust spoon contact depth downward
Test adjusted spoon grasp with small lift and hold
Lift spoon clear of holder slowly while monitoring grip
Turn held spoon bowl left and bring it behind beans
Lower spoon bowl behind coffee beans for controlled sweep toward jar
Angle spoon edge down to tabletop behind beans
Sweep beans gently toward jar opening at table edge
Raise spoon to inspect transfer and remaining beans
Reposition spoon behind remaining beans and lower sweeping edge
Raise hand away from lid and tip spoon bowl down to table
Set accidental lid contact down and release to regrasp spoon cleanly
Support lid and spoon on tabletop and slide open fingers away
Approach spoon handle at its new position clear of lid
Use empty closed fingertips to gather the two separated remaining beans without disturbing lid
Park entangled utensil and lid away from beans, fully release and withdraw
Position now-empty fingertips behind rightmost remaining bean
Guide separated bean toward jar with slow fingertip sweep
Correct lateral alignment behind the right bean
Push right bean back toward edge along its centerline
Center jar below right bean and finish its sweep over edge
Align a small pinch directly around the remaining right bean
Lower fingertips to bean contact depth
Center fingertip ends over bean rather than behind it
Deepen centered bean pinch slightly
Use broad side of horizontal fingers as a scraper behind remaining beans
Sweep remaining beans with broad finger sides into the jar
Lower scraping edge to actual tabletop height and repeat sweep
Tilt fingertips down to reach beans while keeping palm above tabletop
Align the low scraper tip laterally with right bean before sweeping
Sweep aligned tip across right bean toward jar

Withdraw filled jar from under edge, lift and place upright on tabletop

Center open gripper above tilted lid with reachable base placement

alignment.method: Recorded nonterminal execution chunks in order, one video frame per returned state; frame counts checked against each encoded video. The terminal result has no additional video frame.

scope: Complete archived public tool-call sequence and initial task prompt. Response summaries are preserved; the execution video is not a reconstruction of all model input images.
